First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 1}f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 1}\,(\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡t}{t-1}) \\ {lim}_{t\to 1}\,(\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi t}{t}) \\ {lim}_{t\to 1}\,(\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi t}{t})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 1}\,(\frac{(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)^{′}}{(t-1)^{′}}) \\ {lim}_{t\to 1}\,(\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi t}{t}) \\ {lim}_{t\to 1}\,(\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi t}{t})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 1}\,(\frac{1}{t}) \\ \frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi }{1} \\ \frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi }{1}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Note that for the first component of ${lim}_{t\to 1}f(t)$ we used L'Hopital's Rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 1}g(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 1}\,\frac{{t}^{2}-2t+1}{t+1} \\ {lim}_{t\to 1}\,\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡t+t}{t+1} \\ {lim}_{t\to 1}\,\frac{{e}^{t+1}}{t+1}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{1}^{2}-2\cdot 1+1}{1+1} \\ \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡1+1}{1+1} \\ \frac{{e}^{1+1}}{1+1}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{{e}^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 1}[f(t)\cdot g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 1}f(t)\cdot {lim}_{t\to 1}g(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{{e}^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =1\cdot 0+(-2)\cdot \frac{1}{2}+0\cdot \frac{{e}^{2}}{2} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
